column3: I read my wife's WhatsApp while she was fast asleep
I shouldn't have, but I knew something was wrong and it was running deep
For weeks she'd been somewhere else, at dinner, in the car
Fourteen years together and she'd never felt so far
One message to her best friend Mira lit up in the dark
He's 44, he moves like he's 70, there's nothing, not a spark
I put the phone back where it was and lay there on the floor
And waited for the morning like I'd never waited before
The worst part wasn't that she said it, it was that she was right
Three years of back pain, eleven hours at a desk, two hours standing in the local every night
I'd come home and hit the floor, too tired to talk, too sore to hold her tight
At my cousin's sangeet I sat on a plastic chair
While she danced with everyone and I just wasn't there
Our anniversary dinner, I cancelled, said that I was tired, I was always tired
Painkillers every night, sprays that smell like a hospital ward
Balms that burned for ten minutes, physio at 800 a session, more than I could afford
Thousands of rupees gone and nothing left to show
It took my sleep, then it took my fire
It took the man she used to admire
Pain don't just hurt your back, it's true
It took my sleep, my strength, then it took her too
There was an uncle in Building C, 55 at least
Smashing shuttles every morning like his back was 25
While I watched him from my balcony, barely half alive
One day inside the lift I asked him, "Uncle, what are you using?"
He laughed, went up to his flat, came back with a small amber bottle in his hand
Warm it, rub it, throw the sprays out, understand?
That night she watched me warm it in my palms and didn't say a word
No burning, no hospital smell, it just went deep right where it hurt
Night three, I slept straight through, the first time in months
Week two, I got out of bed without that groan, not once
Week four, I took the station stairs two at a time
Month two, I asked her out to walk on Marine Drive, and she took my hand this time
A few Sundays later I was making chai at dawn
She was on the phone with Mira and I heard her going on
I don't know what's happened Mira, he's the man I married again
It gave me back my sleep, it gave me back my fire
I'm the man again that she used to admire
